title: Chapter 105 — Purchasing, Programs & Merchandise Planning
intro: How the floor gets stocked and the feedback loop into purchasing.

sections.title: How the Floor Gets Stocked
sections.content:
Purchasing decisions drive everything you sell. The buyer or merchandise planner decides which brands to carry, which models to display, how much to stock, and when to bring in new product.

As a salesperson, you have more floor intelligence than anyone in the purchasing office. You know which models customers ask for that you do not carry. You know which displays get ignored. You know which products generate the most complaints.

Feed that intelligence back. 'I have had three customers this month ask for the Bosch 800 series in black stainless and we do not have it on display. Can we get one?' That feedback loop makes the floor better for everyone.

sections.title: Manufacturer Programs
sections.content:
Every major manufacturer runs dealer programs with volume rebates, display incentives, and marketing support. Understanding these programs helps you sell smarter.

Package rebates reward customers for buying multiple qualifying pieces from the same brand. Know which packages qualify and present them proactively.

Spiffs are manufacturer bonuses for selling specific products. Use them ethically — recommend the spiff product only when it is genuinely the right fit.

Co-op marketing funds support local advertising. If your store runs a promotion featuring a specific brand, the manufacturer may fund part of the advertising cost.
